title: ChatGPT for Good? On Opportunities and Challenges of Large Language Models for Education
extended_summary:
This position paper examines the opportunities and challenges of large language models (LLMs), especially ChatGPT, for education. Rather than evaluating a specific classroom intervention, it surveys potential uses of LLMs for learning, teaching, assessment, feedback, content generation, and educational technology design, while emphasizing risks such as bias, plagiarism, overreliance, privacy, and the difficulty of distinguishing machine-generated from human-generated text.

The paper discusses applications across educational levels and roles, including primary, secondary, tertiary, and professional learning, with particular attention to teachers’ uses of LLMs for lesson planning, personalized feedback, assessment support, and professional development. It also considers broader human-AI interaction issues such as transparency, fact checking, continuous human oversight, and the need for critical thinking and digital literacy when integrating LLMs into education.

The main conclusion is that LLMs have substantial promise for enhancing educational experiences and supporting teachers, but their adoption should be cautious, ethical, and human-centered. The authors argue for strong governance, verification practices, bias mitigation, privacy protections, and ongoing human monitoring, and they recommend that education systems develop competencies and curricula that help learners and educators use these tools responsibly.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a position paper and grey literature-style conceptual review rather than an empirical study. It provides recommendations and cites prior work, but does not present a controlled methodology or original outcome evaluation.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has broad relevance for education practice and policy, especially around human oversight and verification of LLM output, but it reports no original effect estimates. Its impact is therefore important conceptually, yet empirically unclear.

interventions.use_case: position paper on educational uses of large language models and ChatGPT for student support, teacher assistance, lesson planning, feedback generation, and instructional workflows in education

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that LLMs can support reading and writing through summaries, explanations, grammar/style suggestions, and feedback, but also warns that generated text may be inaccurate, biased, or plagiarized. These claims are conceptual rather than based on a new empirical study, so no effect size or sample size is reported.
finding.measure: Conceptual discussion of reading and writing support, grammar/style correction, summaries, and feedback quality

finding.finding_summary: A major theme is that LLMs may help build critical thinking, problem-solving, curiosity, and fact-checking skills when used as a supplement, but may also weaken them if learners rely on model output uncritically. The paper offers mitigation strategies such as verification, human review, and curriculum design, but does not report empirical estimates.
finding.measure: Conceptual discussion of critical thinking, problem-solving, fact-checking, and curiosity

finding.finding_summary: The paper repeatedly claims that LLMs can reduce teacher workload by automating or semi-automating lesson planning, personalized feedback, assessment, quiz generation, and text revision. It cites prior work suggesting grading effort could be reduced by up to 85% in large courses, but this position paper itself does not run a new evaluation.
finding.measure: Teacher workload, grading effort, and efficiency of feedback/lesson-material generation

finding.finding_summary: The paper’s core contribution is a policy and governance argument: LLMs in education require human oversight, transparency, privacy protections, bias mitigation, and guidance on verification and integrity. It frames adoption as promising but contingent on institutional controls and responsible deployment rather than presenting empirical effects.
finding.measure: Governance, privacy, bias mitigation, oversight, and responsible deployment considerations
